confidence_notes: Food and coffee anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living figures found in a web search. Expatica cites Numbeo data from June 2026: cappuccino about EUR 2.21, 0.5 L draught beer about EUR 3.13, inexpensive meal about EUR 12.49 and mid-range meal for two about EUR 46.85. Euro prices were converted to USD at about 1.10 USD per EUR, which I worked out from the RBA AUD/USD and AUD/EUR rates reported for 18 Nov 2026. The beer anchor is set a little below the 0.5 L price because a typical restaurant serving in Andalusia is usually smaller (a cana or tercio). Cocktail and wine prices were not searched directly. They are estimated from how local drink prices compare with beer and from Andalusian norms: a glass of house wine costs about EUR 2.5-3.5 and a cocktail about EUR 7-9. Accommodation prices are my own overall estimates for July, which is a hot, shoulder-to-low demand month in Cordoba, and were not checked against live listings. The hotel and hostel anchors are less certain than the restaurant anchors. Sources: https://www.expatica.com/es/cost-of-living/cordoba/ ; https://livingcost.org/cost/cordoba/madrid ; https://mylifeelsewhere.com/cost-of-living/spain/cordoba-c8722
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Cordoba-specific aggregated food prices. Accommodation is benchmarked against similar Andalusian heritage cities such as Granada and Seville, scaled down because Cordoba has slightly lower prices and weaker summer demand.
